Thus, O lords of sages, has been told the greatness of the venerable Guru, who is the protector and the Lord— the essence of all the Vedas. Whoever, with steady mind and supreme devotion, reads or hears this, the Lord bestows even greater grace upon him.
It bestows the desired object. || 123 ||

[Thus, in the extensive narrative of the venerable *Bhaviṣyapurāṇa*, which accords with the words of the hosts of Pramathas, whose nature is to uplift people submerged in the impurities of the Kali age, and which concerns the divine play of Liṅga;]
The twenty-third chapter, titled "The Account of the Description of the Greatness of the Lord’s Service and His Meal Performed by Basaveśvara.
Now begins the twenty-fourth chapter.
Salutations to the illustrious Nandikeśvara.
Sūta said:
Those who have shaken off all defects through meditation on the pair of feet of the Lord Siddha Śrī Vīranātha;

who are free from concern for speech, dress, and the like; whose limbs are devoted to the worship of the *liṅga* at the city of Gurucarapura; who seek liberation, possess pure disposition, and are detached, being devoid of attachment to their own bodies, wealth, and desires.
Let the devotees listen to the vast and noble narrative of the Lord’s divine play, which is the refuge of all masters.
Then, having beheld him who stood near the footstool of the assembly of all the Śambhus, for the sake of attaining the realization of the *Śivarahasya*:

The Teacher of the World said: "O, listen to the essence of the scriptures, which is the supreme dissolution of the mind; for without that, there is no attainment of oneness with Śiva for human beings."
The mind creates everything and indeed causes it to grow;
that very mind, reflected in the mirror of the ego-sense (*ahaṃkriyā*) as it becomes solidified, appears in embodied form.
It is surely this [mind] alone that is the cause of both bondage and liberation in the world.
One should completely destroy that [impurity] here, whether it be firm or loose, by means of gradual stages. || 3 ||
Without the dissolution of the mind, there is no arising of the realization of the Self as Śiva;
without the experience of Śiva, Māyā does not come to an end;
and without the bliss of non-dual Śiva, which strikes at the very root of the mass of darkness, [liberation is not attained].
This Śāmbhava [teaching] is not established for those who are awakened by the hosts of Śiva.
Having heard what was spoken by the Guru, Basava, the chief minister,
said: "O Lord Allama, for the sake of dispelling all our doubts, these Gaṇas, through service at your feet,
[desire to hear] the supreme reality of the Śivarahasya."
They dwell all around to awaken [the world]; please favor us with your instruction.
Having heard the words of the sage Vāsava with great respect, the Lord and Guru,
whose horizons were suffused with a gentle smile and the light of his intense radiance, spoke: "The body, when it becomes capable of worshipping the chosen *liṅga*, is supremely purifying."
The mind is always perfectly pure through the constant union with the auspicious *liṅga*.
O leaders of the Gaṇas, this great vow of yours, observed with excellent conduct, is the means to liberation; what further instruction could I possibly give here?
Whatever is desired, seen, or likewise remembered within the self—all that is complete.
May there always be auspiciousness for you, solely through the power of Śiva’s grace. || 7 ||
Having thus spoken words of blessing for the expansion of the host of lords and gurus, and saying,
"I shall return again after wandering about," he then rose up with speed and departed.
That lord of the rod firmly grasped the pair of the Lord’s lotus feet.
Having heard Basaveśa’s prayer, the Lord spoke with affection to the Gaṇas:
"O ocean of the Guru’s mercy, our minds are filled with both fear and devotion."
Having warded off here the doubts regarding the state of awakening, in order to protect [us] and to lead us to the further shore of the ocean of this endless existence,
we have come for refuge to You alone, O Śrī Guru, the bearer of the burden. 9.
O Guru, favor the path of liberation with diligence; for nothing else increases together with prosperity for those of ruined intellect, as their delusion is extreme.
Indeed, whatever ritual action is performed by one desiring a fruit, it [only leads to further bondage].
Indeed, it is only by those of dull intellect that this is enjoyed for so long by the common folk. 10.
Therefore, O dear one, enough with the attainment of worldly power or even with actions that yield fruit;
rather, [attain it] through the pure and uninterrupted meditation upon the Śiva-liṅga.
O True Guru, having placed our feet firmly upon the final path and having warded off the suffering caused by coming and going, protect us. 11.
Then, as Basavanātha made his request, the Lord, looking upon the Gaṇas with compassion and considering them to be qualified,
spoke for the purpose of imparting instruction in the knowledge of reality.
Having reached the further shore of devotion and ritual action, you have attained fulfillment;
you have sought the incomparable perfection of actionlessness (naiṣkarmyasiddhi) in order to reach the supreme state. || 13 ||
"I shall speak only the secret of the reality of Śiva for you who possess the requisite authority;
listen with attentive minds," he said, and having thus addressed them, began to speak immediately. 14.

The Lord said: "If one contemplates in the heart that the entire visible universe is false, and understands it to be merely illusion according to the Śruti, then that illusion shall perish; thereafter, he becomes a conqueror of the senses."
When the agitation born of the senses has perished, the perverse pursuit of sense-objects will cease; having lost all scent of objects, one becomes a conqueror of the enemy. || 15 ||
Just as, after the husks and other impurities have been removed, one might again winnow the stone-grains with discrimination so that the heap of rice remains here by itself,
so too, when the fluctuations of the mind manifested through evil intentions have been diminished...
From that, one shall proceed to increase, possessing the splendor of most pure and excellent knowledge. || 16 ||
When full awakening has occurred and the scent of sense objects has been destroyed, that great duality—namely, "this is to be meditated upon" and "this is to be accepted"—perishes.
Indeed, it is the mind that is the cause of conceptual constructions; therefore, in its conquest, [all duality vanishes].
This phenomenal world is false; it consists of the empire of immortality.
That which causes the three states to revolve through the three bodies, constantly bringing the three qualities and the three individual souls into union;
it is the instruction on the secret reality of Śiva bestowed by the Lord upon the assemblies [of disciples].
In the great cycle of existence, which abounds in the pleasures and pains of heaven and hell, one should conquer the mind; that which transcends this triad is Paraśiva. || 18 ||
As long as the mind is prone to outward expansion, this entire phenomenal world remains real; indeed, there is no talk of liberation at all.
It surely creates the state of divinity, the state of humanity, and even the state of being an animal.
Or when will that king of the Vasus not become motionless in the face of victory? 19.
If the mind, having abandoned all external wandering through its inwardness, becomes dissolved in the reality of the inner self and attains a stable state,
then the world indeed becomes illusory, and one becomes filled with bliss.
O Basava, he who possesses self-knowledge is himself wise and is even the teacher of teachers.
If this entire world, which appears externally in the form of visible objects, were perceived within one's own mind, then the mind itself would be the locus of unreality;
for if one is capable of making that [external world] abide within, one must follow after it.
O Basava, know that such a person who acts according to his own whims is a mere beast among men. || 21 ||
Alas! The noose of illusion is desire; if the mind is bound by it, the entire mass of afflictions arises.
Bound by that, this victorious worldly existence incurs even greater fear.
O Basava, he who has transcended hope is this very person, free from fault and with rebirth destroyed.

As long as the individual soul (*jīva*) does not abandon its own mental constructs— fashioned by conceptualization such as "may this be mine" or "may this not be mine"— due to its state of being a bound animal (*paśu*),
it shall not reach the destruction of the affliction caused by the multitude of enemies such as delusion (*moha*) and the rest.
Therefore, upon the abandonment of that [duality], one becomes Basava; for he is indeed the eternal Paśupati.
This mind, unable to find stability anywhere even for half a moment, constantly recollects all objects; indeed, there is no counting its cycles.
This is its very nature, and by that alone, the entirety [of its activity] prevails.
The intermingling of fragrances reflected through attachment to worldly proliferation. || 24 ||
"Or rather, this inner self, having attained growth through latent impressions (vāsanās) and being moved by desire, falls into delusion;
he who, having restrained that mind, swallows it up with steady intellect—he alone is blessed, O Basava," so he spoke when thus addressed. (25)
Bhāskara said: "You have stated that one should devour the mind; how can the mind become a voracious devourer of the mind?
O Guru, if it were to abandon its fickleness and remain steady, then let that steadiness be what constitutes 'devouring'. (26)
To Basaveśvara, the Lord gave this reply:

"O Master, if it is your thought that another indeed devours [the self], then is he the individual soul (jīva), the inner self (antarātman), or the supreme self (parātman)? Tell me. Being thus addressed, He spoke as follows. (27)
The Lord said: "The Self, the Inner Self, and likewise the Supreme Self—these are declared to be the one Great Lord and nothing else.
The Self is threefold, conforming to the internal organs; through the superimposition of those qualities upon itself, it becomes the individual soul (jīva). (28)

When that very inner self becomes extracted, pure, and capable of grasping the mind, then, having attained oneness with the Supreme Self, it shines forth as full, itself a solid mass of the bliss of Śiva. (29)
As long as the mind does not come under one's control, one must strive with effort to restrain it.
Thinking "I shall swallow the mind," one should surely swallow that mind itself by means of effort, having warded off its power.
Indeed, by uniting with hundreds of illusory modes of existence, it inevitably torments those who seek its realization;
therefore, having struck it down and winnowed it through fortitude, the cessation of delusion is truly its devouring.
"He who devours the mind, whose power is great, and who is far removed from transformation—he is indeed of noble form.
Having heard these words of the Lord, "He cannot be described," the best of sages, Channa, spoke with a hidden intention.
(32) Channabasava said:
O Guru, for the practitioner to destroy the mind, there must indeed be an object of focus;
O Sovereign Lord, by teaching us such an object here, you have fulfilled our purpose.
The Lord said:
Having heard Channa’s words, the Teacher said to him: "Your question is not indeed substantial;
nevertheless, like the moon at the tip of a branch, this is a means for the sake of awakening the ignorant. (34)
The various types of objects of perception (*lakṣya*) have been taught in many ways in the Śaiva scriptures of Yoga and Āgama;
yet that which is perceived within, without, and in between, exists only as a secondary reflection of the inner consciousness (*pratīcchā*).
This is not an object of perception through descriptions of objects to be perceived; for it is perceived precisely by being beyond all perception.
It is the singular object of focus, a dense mass of Being, Consciousness, Bliss, and Joy; having cast aside Māyā, it is perceived solely as the Self. (36)
The Lord of Guha favored Channaghana with a sidelong glance and the essence of his nectar-like speech.
Just as iron is drawn to a magnet, so did the Vasus, through their longing for him, draw near to that youth.
In the meantime, Mācayadevanātha, having prostrated before the pair of lotus feet of Śrīnātha, [spoke].
Mācayāya gave his reply to the Lord:
with limbs bowed in devotion, dressed in modest attire, and having realized the truth, he posed a question.
38 Maṇivālamācayadeva said:

That reality which is most beyond the reach of the words of the Vedas, which is difficult to attain through meditation, which is not an object of contemplation, which is devoid of limbs, and which remains invisible to the eyes; [that is this].
"O Lord, having understood that void which is the supreme reality, how does one attain eternity through great devotion? Please tell me," he asked; thus addressed, the Guru spoke with certainty.
The Lord said: That supreme Brahman, whose nature is truth, knowledge, and bliss, is stainless and full; it exists everywhere, yet it cannot be perceived by external senses anywhere.

As long as there is the entire burden of the dullness of illusion—the great conceit of identifying with the body—there is no possibility whatsoever regarding the reality of things, for this visible world is indeed perishable. (40)
The three states—waking, dreaming, and deep sleep—are ever-woven into the three bodies;
they repeatedly cause the individual soul to wander, depriving it of the knowledge of its own Self.

Helpless within the net of evil intentions and conceptual constructions, one who has fallen into the sleep of saṃsāra will perish; therefore, by means of self-restraint, one should first conquer these three states.
He who is ever mounted upon that which is called the Fourth, the Innate, shall destroy this triad that is the cause of the state of the bound soul.
Thus, through his state as Maheśvara, he becomes full of awakening within himself and attains the ultimate reality by means of the experience of the bliss of the Supreme Self. || 42 ||
He who seeks Śiva, casting off the delusion that "the three bodies are myself," remains as pure consciousness alone.

"O learned one, having realized the most subtle reality of Vedānta, that person attains eternity; it is I myself who am that person. Then, having heard the words of his guru, Mācayadeva’s mind became fixed right there upon the supreme reality. Having abandoned all latent impressions (*vāsanā*), he experienced the bliss of the Self, which is truth and knowledge, remaining composed in meditation.
It is so. || 44 ||
Like a lunar stone struck by a mass of moonbeams, Maṇivāla’s mind was made blissful by the essence of intense, innate joy.
Having understood this, all the hosts led by Basava spoke to the sovereign Guru in order to remove his doubt: || 45 ||
Basava and the other hosts of Pramathas said:
"O Lord, if the body, mind, senses, and all else are unreal, then, O God, they are not external to the Self, just like a pot and such objects."
In that case, what effort indeed could there be in providing a rebuttal? The discussion regarding the liberation of Videha is futile;
it is merely a response given by the Lord to Basava and his followers.
If everything—external organs and the like—simply does not exist, then how can this person be bound? For one who is unattached, what bondage could there be?
"If there is no bondage, how could there be a desire for liberation on his part?"—when they had spoken thus, the Lord replied once more: || 47 ||
The Lord said: "Listen, O multitudes of devotees! Illusion—endlessly treacherous and characterized by neither existence nor non-existence—is certainly not to be overcome by logic."
Constantly imagining even non-existent things as real, she brings even a man who is free from attachment under her own power. || 48 ||
Indeed, the entire collection of visible phenomena, which constitutes its effect, is like a dream-world and does not exist in reality.
Until awakening, this world appears as if it truly exists, just as silver appears in a mother-of-pearl shell; such is its falsity.
Therefore, in order to ward off the entanglement of beginningless delusion, one should cultivate devotion for the lotus feet of Maheśvara.
This Supreme Self, situated upon the peak of the three-footed *praṇava*, has as His foot the entire multitude of beings within the belly of the universe.
Or rather, like gentle breezes resorting to sandalwood trees in spring, all the Gaṇas took refuge with the minister Basava.

Those who have come under the power of the yoga of true knowledge seek only the oneness of the *liṅga* (the supreme reality), and not any other state within their inner being; for Māyā does not abandon those who are skilled in the discourse of the Vāgbrahma (the Word-Brahman), nor is the realization of non-duality possible without the grace of Abhava (Śiva).
Without devotion, Paraśiva does not show compassion; and without the immobility of the mind, there is no devotion. || 52 ||
Therefore, one should forcefully and suddenly conquer passion and hatred; from that alone does the intellect become steady, and from that, devotion arises.

O lords of sages, those whose intellects are established in the jewel-like state beyond conceptualization and volition do not resort to the web of discursive thoughts in order to make that [state] perfectly stable.
One should not include within it the inclusion of name-and-form and their activities, nor that insatiable egoity which leads to the end of suffering.
Thus, having abandoned the phenomena of the body, vital breath, mind, and so forth, the wise one transcends the ocean of delusion.
O Vasu, let it be for now; for the sake of protecting the world, you have revealed the true essence of the Vedic doctrine under the guise of a question.

You are the omniscient teacher of the three worlds; there is no one equal to you in the world, O Friend of the Universe, through your devotion to the aesthetic essence of the oneness of the *liṅga* and the state of *samarasa*. 55.
The Lord’s praise of Basaveśa and Basava’s reply:
"O Basava, who here is able to describe the incomparable devotion of yours to Śiva, the Supreme Reality?
O Great-Souled One, all things dwell within you, the conscious Self; yet you shine forth as if possessed of attributes."
Unsurpassed by qualities. || 56 ||
Having thus heard the words of his lordly guru, he bowed his head to the pair of the guru’s lotus feet.
With palms joined in reverence and his face slightly bowed, Basavādhipati spoke again to the God with devotion.

Having attributed preeminence to this one who knows but little and possesses a multitude of faults, or else having cast him once again into the pit of great delusion within the ocean of saṃsāra— what have you done?

O venerable Guru, it is not at all fitting to calculate the coming and going [of the breath]; through the instruction of the true reality, make me one with the flavor of equanimity by means of right vision. 58.
Just as that very coconut which is impossible even to crack with one's teeth is swallowed and digested by an elephant,
so too you, having swallowed all principles (tattvas), appear as if bodiless despite being embodied.
For we are all indeed cattle bound by your noose; you, O God, are Paśupati, the ancient Puruṣa.

"O best of noble gurus, it is through your compassion alone that a living being attains the state of Maheśvara," he said; and the Lord replied: "You are the very embodiment of the science of the supreme self (adhyātmavidyā), and you stand as one who possesses full authority."
For the purpose of illuminating the tradition in the world, [this was taught] concerning the illustrious Guru and the disciple. (61)
This heart-pleasing knowledge, consistent with Vedānta, has been explained according to the prescribed rules.
O Basava, they are always inlaid within your peaceful heart.
For my soul is exceedingly pleased because it has come into your presence.
This is not a sequence of hymns; I do not know that which is your vital point.
Those whose five sheaths are accumulated from the various qualities of the five elements conquered through meditation on the five-syllabled mantra;
Those seeking refuge constantly take shelter in you, the worthy protector; today you have become the crown of the great hosts of those who bear the moon upon their crests.
O noble Basava, it is your very contemplation that makes one a Guru and likewise makes one a Linga;
that same contemplation of yours also creates a Jangama. I swear by you, for you are truly the embodied form of the Unborn (Brahman). 65.
That very memory of the mind within yourself is Sā; Maṇivālanātha is the true Vīrabasava;
he is Jñapti, the wise one who moves through existence (bhācara), renowned as Viveka; likewise, Śīla is Arpaṇa-muni, and Kinnara is your limb.
The mutual request and consolation between Basava and Eshalla:
"O noble Basava, you are indeed the very embodiment of consciousness, for you are the personification of all those devoted to Śiva."
"Who indeed on earth is able to praise your great majesty?"— being addressed thus,
Basava spoke to him.
Basava said:
O Lord Allama, by the mere service of your lotus feet, and solely through your compassion, I now attain the state of one who has fulfilled his purpose.
Does your word become useless, being superior even to the end of the scriptures?
Nevertheless, seeking refuge, I beg a boon from some god. || 68 ||

Having graced this entire succession of devotees on earth with the splendor of your sidelong glance and through auspicious initiation, [may you lead them] to the state of oneness with the supreme Śambhu.
Having been addressed thus—"O Lord, please be gracious; protect me, having utterly cast aside the succession of birth and death"—the Guru spoke to him.
The Lord said: "O Basava, let it be so; by means of the power of your great genius, may the auspiciously arisen, virtuous, and worthy attendants of Śiva be established."
For me, who has been fulfilled by being taught the reality of the oneness of Vimalaśiva, my effort would indeed be like that of one who has turned gold into something fragrant.

Just as awakening brings happiness to one whose mind is distressed by the experience of suffering in a dream, so too [is it for those] whose dull intellects are obscured by latent impressions manifested through the five [senses].

Then, at the request of Basava for the sake of bestowing grace, the illustrious Guru made all of them his disciples, instructing them with words such as, "May the path to nirvāṇa arise from awakening through compassion. || 71 ||
In accordance with whatever pleases the heart of each individual, and in that manner, step by step.
Reflecting upon each respective office and making it understood, the true guru instructed them. || 72 ||
Causing one to abandon attachment to the body, mind, wealth, and delusion, [it leads] to pure devotion and awakening.
Establishing a profound instruction on right discernment within the limbs and the Liṅga, he brought them to a state of non-minuteness.
Having cast aside the distinction of "I" and "you," You compassionately made the multitude of Your devotees whose hearts were absorbed in the oneness with Your Liṅga.

Having made the non-dual Brahman manifest through hundreds of scriptural texts, he rendered it directly present in his heart, though previously it had been beyond perception, by virtue of his piercing insight.
Having dispelled the triad consisting of the knower, knowledge, and the known— which is impossible to see, describe, or even perceive—

that Lord caused this Basavādhipati to experience the reality of Brahman, which is full, stainless, uninterrupted, eternally true, and established him in this supreme, incomparable, and illusory-less state.
A Description of the Bliss of Unity with the Liṅga for the Gaṇas of Śiva:
At that moment, by virtue of their innate experience and through the gracious side-glance of the Lord, the Gaṇas of Śiva enjoyed the bliss of unity with the Liṅga. || 76 ||
Just as the branches of a tree attain growth through the watering of its roots, so too [does it proceed] from the root that is Basaveṃdra.
In the same way, the Gaṇas, relying on the grace of their Lord and being firmly established in the supreme reality, quickly attained perfect meditative absorption. || 77 ||

Just as various multicolored masses of dense clouds in the sky disperse by the force of the wind, so too did the illusions within the hearts of Bhaṇḍāri, Vīrabhadra, Vasavādhipa, Māca, Ārya, Nāga, Ambikā, Haṭha, Padārpaṇa, Kinnara, and Ārya vanish through the power of the Lord’s instruction.
Chanda and the other attendants of Śiva, having attained liberation while living through the grace of their Lord, dwelt there in happiness. || 79 ||
Thus, O lords of all sages, this treatise on the playful manifestation of the Fortune of Liberation, which is the holy life of the illustrious Guru, has been declared to you.
The Lord bestows even greater desired objects upon that man who recites [this] with supreme devotion and a pure mind. (80)

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "The Path of Instruction on the Dissolution of the Mind," within the *Prabhuliṅgalīlā*— the expansive narrative of the venerable *Bhaviṣyatpurāṇa* composed in accordance with the words of the *Pramatha* hosts, and characterized by its intent to uplift people submerged in the impurities of the Kali age.
[Now begins the twenty-fifth chapter.
Homage to the illustrious Nandikeśvara.
Sūta said:
The lords of sages, devoted to the service of the feet of the illustrious Siddhavīreśvara and delighting in the knowledge of Śiva.
"May those who are far from ignorance and thick with devotion to Hara listen to the divine play of the Lord in his form as the Liṅga.
Thus did the Lord [address] all the hosts of devotees through their steadfastness in the oneness of the Liṅga.
Having fulfilled their purpose, he spent some time together with them.
Then, having departed from the city of Kalyāṇa, the great teacher—
For the sake of bestowing grace upon his devotees, he wandered over this earth.
By virtue of the grace of the unity of the Liṅga, the Lord [bestowed this] upon all the assemblies of devotees.
Having withdrawn his inscrutable illusion, he bestowed liberation by means of a sidelong glance.
In the continuous expanse of the lotus-pool of the minds of those devoted to the virtuous.
The Blessed One, the beloved of Lord Nallama, became a swan.
There, on that sovereign mountain Kailāsa, dwells the glorious one who bears the crescent moon.
He reported the entire account to that great goddess.
Having heard the entire account of the Lord's deeds from Śeṣabhūṣaṇa,
The queen, her heart filled with joy, questioned him.
O Lord of my life, by your command, that sattvic power of mine [is at your disposal].
I have sent forth your own pure consciousness.
That conduct of his is not known to me; instruct me thoroughly, O Lord.
Thus entreated, Śaṅkara spoke to her.
Listen, O lotus-eyed one, to this natural grace of yours.
Then Queen Akvā became one whose mind was filled with splendor through her divine power.
But the Lord, pure consciousness, is my self, the root cause.
For the sake of protecting the world, there appeared a king of yogins named Mallama.
She is blissful through the knowledge of the identity with the *liṅga* attained by His grace.
Then the Great Goddess went to Śrīgirī, which is inhabited by yogis.
Those who were portions of the lords of the Pramathas became Channabasava and the others.
Having descended to the surface of the earth, they fixed their minds upon the Lord.
Those various leaders of the Pramathas were born within their respective lineages.
Having realized the oneness of the Liṅga as instructed by the Lord, they became seekers of liberation.
With the wealth obtained through various bodily efforts, one should honor the gurus, the elders, and the lords.
Constantly worshipping [him], they attained liberation while living. || 15 ||
By my command, the omniscient Śrī Nandīśa is a second Śambhu.
In order to uplift my devotion on earth, he became the son of Mādāmbā.
This is the life story of Basava, as told by Śiva;
that high-minded one named Basava was the son of Mādana and Ārādhyā.
He attained the imperial sovereignty of the ministers of the Lord of Kalyāṇanagara. || 17 ||
This [work] possesses the power of piercing through mere contact; it dispels the doctrines of opposing disputants.
He was a supreme believer who became the restorer of the Vīraśaiva lineage. || 18 ||
He is the crest-jewel of my devotees, the bestower of desired objects upon those who seek them.
He has made his mind, body, and wealth entirely dependent upon his devotees.
In the course of a pleasant conversation with countless hosts of Śiva’s attendants.
Passing his time, this wise man remained in the city of Kalyāṇapaṭṭana.
The extraordinary majesty of the Lord was [proclaimed] by the excellent visiting ascetics.
Having heard that, King Basava became one whose heart was fixed upon her. || 21 ||
When will the beloved of Lord Mallama come to my house?
When will all the doubts in our hearts be severed by his grace? (22)
When [will there be] the supreme sequence of the secret worship of the Guru, Caresa, and Arcā?
And the true Guru will instruct [the disciple] in the union of the body with the Prāṇaliṅga.
Thus, along with his hosts of devotees, Basaveśa [observed] the rising of the moon.
Like a cakora bird, he longed with eager longing for the sight of his lord.
Then the Lord of Allama, out of affection, held him in his heart like a cow her calf.
Having recollected [this], the Teacher of the World arrived at the City of Virtue.
Having personally performed the rites of worship along with his devotees headed by Basava, he...
The Blessed One bestowed upon him unwavering self-knowledge.
Having realized that supreme reality which is inexpressible, the Guru [taught] the Gaṇas.
He brought about the perfect awakening of those whose true nature was latent within the heart-center (cilli). || 27 ||
The supreme Lord of Vīraśaiva, manifesting everything within the liṅga.
He bestowed his grace upon Sāra and the other lords of the Gaṇas, such as Basava. || 28 ||
When the Lord of Gods had spoken thus, the daughter of the King of Mountains [replied].
Filled with apprehension, she questioned Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the world.
From God arises the all-pervading Lama, who is devoid of name, form, and the like.
There are six philosophical systems regarding the universal; how can there be devotion to Vīraśaiva? (30)
Śiva said to the Great Goddess: "Listen, O beloved of my life."
Know this to be the supreme non-duality and the glory of Vīraśaivism. || 31 ||
It consists of the forms of Raudra, Vaiṣṇava, Daurga, Ārka, Skānda, and Gāṇeśvara.
The six systems of thought have been established by the Tantrikas as being distinct and separate from one another. || 32 ||
Among the six systems of thought, the Vīraśaiva doctrine holds predominance;
it is dualistic in nature, contrary to Vedānta, and inconsistent.
It bestows the fruits of dharma, artha, and kāma, and is the sole means for attaining each respective world.
Because it is a cause for returning again, that is not liberation in any way whatsoever.
However, the cause of bondage for men is their destiny to various worlds.
Without casting aside the fruit of karma, one accomplishes the stainless nectar.
O Goddess, there are six matas, which are primarily concerned with the knowledge of differentiation.
As for the view of the Mīmāṃsakas regarding the section on ritual action (karmakāṇḍa), O blameless one:
For that [action] is primarily characterized by violence and yields fruits such as heaven, hell, and so forth.
Men blinded by intoxication, though desiring heaven, commit acts of violence.
Śaṅkara does not favor those fools who harm living beings. || 37 ||
O beloved, without the grace of Śambhu, compassion does not flow forth.
Without the grace of Śiva, liberation is cast far away; of this there is no doubt. || 38 ||
Therefore, through the very attainment of freedom from action (naiṣkarmya), one should find delight in Vīraśaivism.
For Vīraśaivism is established by the Vedānta as the sole means for attaining liberation. || 39 ||
As long as there is a mind that perceives duality, saṃsāra will never cease.
O Daughter of the Mountain, non-duality (advaita), known as Vīraśaiva, is that which sublates all distinctions.
Through the relationship of identity between the limb and the liṅga, a man becomes a Vīraśaiva.
The individual soul is the *aṅga-liṅga* and the Lord is the *īśa*; their union is indeed *saṃgati*. || 41 ||
For the realization of the identity of Śiva and the individual soul is indeed an object unknown to worldly people.
The purport of the scripture is said to reside in that which is unknown and productive of fruit. (42)
O lady, non-duality (advaita), which is accessible through the Vedas alone, is known as Vīraśaiva.
But difference is considered to be worldly, known even to children and cowherds. || 43 ||
Therefore, for those men whose intellects are well-settled through the realization of the Vedānta, [there is no further need].
The minds of the great-souled ones who are dispassionate become fixed upon Vīraśaiva. || 44 ||
Relying upon the knowledge of the identity with the Liṅga, which arises from the dharma proclaimed in Vīraśaivism.
They attain supreme liberation, from which there is no return.
Having looked at the Lord of Life who had spoken thus, the Daughter of the Mountain King—
Out of affection, with her palms joined in reverence, she paid homage and spoke as follows.
The Vīraśaivas, who are non-dualists, are firmly convinced that "I am Brahman."
Or they propitiate you, O Lord, or they remain silent. || 47 ||
O Lord, act for me in such a way that my mind may become free from doubt regarding the description of the true nature of the Vīraśaiva way of life.
Thus questioned, Mahādeva spoke to the woman of excellent complexion.
O auspicious lady, now listen to the righteous Vīraśaiva tradition.
By the mere knowledge of which one attains the unity of Śiva and the individual soul. || 49 ||
In Vīraśaiva, the non-duality of existence and the non-duality of action are praised.
One should contemplate non-duality in the mind, but one should resort to duality in ritual action.
Having completely abandoned external rituals, one should perform the worship of me as prescribed by the rules.
The Vīraśaiva constantly and fully performs all the rites of hospitality. || 51 ||
Having surrendered all action unto me alone, with firm conviction.
The heroic Śaiva, possessing dispassion, does not desire any fruit whatsoever.
Abandoning desire for mind, body, and wealth, one should cherish one's own self, wife, and sons.
He who offers [this] to me is called a Vīraśaiva. || 53 ||
But he who, having abandoned the delusion of the five senses, perceives the end of the lotus [of the heart].
Knowing that nothing else is auspicious, he is a hero and is called a Śaiva. || 54 ||
Worshipping no other gods, they [realized] that there is only one supreme Brahman.
He who perceives only the oneness of the Liṅga is indeed a Vīra-Māheśvara.
At the time of lifting me up, preceded by a visible sign of proof.
He who establishes the ultimate reality is known as a Śāmbhava hero.
He indeed worships me with devotion and never desires any fruit whatsoever.
Even that which is given by me, he does not accept; he is a Vīraśaiva, a sovereign among yogins.
O Noble Lady, one does not abandon the vow once undertaken, even at the cost of one's life.
Endowed with the knowledge of the identity of the Linga, he becomes a Vīraśāmbhava. || 58 ||
Free from the defect of attachment, one should nail the liṅga into the six limbs.
By virtue of the oneness of his beloved with his own life-breath, the yogi is the supreme Vīraśaiva.
Whether it be a birth, a death, or even a period of ritual impurity (sūtaka), none of these shall occur for him.
Through the immersion into Sadāśiva, that yogi is a Vīraśāmbhava. || 60 ||
One should never show cooked food prepared for the sake of Śiva to those bound by worldly existence.
O Maheśvarī, a Vīraśaiva should not give [this] to outsiders.
Who is able to describe the conduct of a Vīraśaiva?
Nor even by Speech herself, nor by the Lord of Speech (Bṛhaspati), nor by Brahmā, or even by Viṣṇu.
"Description of the Greatness of Vīraśaiva":
When her beloved had ceased speaking thus, the consort of Śaṅkara was filled with wonder.
With her body covered in horripilation, she spoke again to that Śaṅkara.
O Lord of Men, those Vīraśaivas are constant wearers of the *liṅga*.
Tell me, how can those things that are without an object appear as if they possess an object? 64.
How is it that those such as these have no sense of "mine" regarding their bodies or mental objects?
When addressed with the words "Command me," Giriśa spoke to Girijā.
Listen with focused attention to the majesty of Vīraśaiva.
The succession of mental fluctuations is attached to the three bodies.
Having completely abandoned the three marks through the three initiations in their respective order.
Furthermore, the wise-minded one, having considered the unity of the limbs and the unity of those [limbs] themselves, [proceeds].
The succession of steps belonging to the devotees of Maheśvara and others.
Having ascended [the throne], preceded by the knowledge of the limbs, the *liṅga*, the face, and the hands.
Equalizing all powers, one should resort to the path of the oneness of the Liṅga.
Like a hand falling into the ocean, or like the wind pervading the sky. || 69 ||
With his three bodies dissolved into his own self like the moon merging into the fire;
The wise one attains the realization of identity with that [reality] through the compassion of the Guru. || 70 ||
Due to his knowledge of the true nature of things, he has no attachment to the body, the sense organs, and so forth.
Even while being watched by those standing at his side, [he remains so] for the yogin who is liberated while living.
Having heard these words of Śambhu and having bowed down, the daughter of the mountain king—
Having understood that secret of existence, she thought, "I have achieved my purpose."
To her who was prostrating like a staff, the Lord, who bears the crescent moon, [spoke].
Embracing her with both arms, he gladdened the beautiful woman.
Having abandoned the envy felt toward those who have conquered illusion, [one should do so] before the Lord of All.
Pārvatī considered this [Śiva] to be the manifest teacher of the world.
The Lord Allama protected all the hosts of our devotees.
Having granted liberation, Umā and Śambhu attained joy in their hearts.
Gaurī and Maheśvara [dwell] on the beautiful summit of Mount Kailāsa, the lord of mountains.
O twice-born ones, they remained there, filled with supreme bliss, engaged in pleasant conversation.

There, by virtue of his grace, he constantly nourished the young and the old, kings, children, the masses of the poor, the wealthy, the virtuous, cows, Brahmins, the entire multitude of living beings, and all classes of society without exception.
The sages' question to Sūta concerning the secret reality:
"O Lord, the entire world is filled with the bliss of Śambhu, endowed with the abundance of all fruits,
and possessed of the wealth of happiness."
Having compassionately favored him, the illustrious Guru, whose form manifests by his own will, purified the earth. || 78 ||
O lords of all sages, this divine play of the illustrious Guru, expanded by the life-stories of his attendants, has been [revealed] through the grace of the sage Vyāsa.
Commanded by the illustrious Maheśa who dwells within the heart-lotus, may this [work], which is conducive to worldly enjoyment and liberation, be efficacious for those who recite it. 79.

Having heard the account of the manifestations and deeds of the Lord as spoken by the Sūta, the lords of sages were tossed about for a long time within the ocean of the nectar of supreme Brahman-bliss.
With a single flavor of bliss, they praised and bowed to him with reverence on all sides; having directly surrendered everything to the Supreme Śiva, they attained liberation while living.
Having heard this wonderful account, the sages looked again at the son of Sūta and, desiring to ask about this secret clearly reflected in their own minds, said: "O Lord..."

"You too, having manifested compassion for the sake of protecting the world, must speak; having reflected in your mind upon the entire meaning of the scriptures as it pertains to yourself," thus he asked without being prompted. || 81 ||
The four-faced one created this entire phenomenal world by the command of the Lord of All.
At the beginning, it was well-spoken by you and by the Vedas, as before: "In the beginning, the Creator created [the world] from his own self. || 82 ||
Within His creation, all living beings, such as gods and humans, desire happiness and liberation.
Since everyone resorts to the Lord of All alone, O Great-Souled One, for what purpose do others seek another sovereign? (83)
And in all those portions of the Purāṇas heard from your own lips here and there.
The stories of those who have taken refuge in the various systems of Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu, and other gods have been told;
likewise, the accounts of the twice-born, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, those born in the natural order (anuloma), and those born in the inverse order (pratiloma).
Likewise, you have heard of those belonging to the stages of life (āśramins), whose duties are distinct and who pursue separate goals.
Among them were those renowned as great-souled ones, who were exclusively devoted to Śiva and sought refuge in him, as well as those who were learned in the Vedas.
They were firmly established in the duties of their respective castes and stages of life, and were likewise consecrated in the state of the formless. || 86 ||
The Lord, the Sovereign of this entire world, has manifested here in person as Vīraśaiva.
For Śruti is the authority regarding all that is possible; O Lord, how can its uniformity be maintained? || 87 ||
For having reflected upon all this, O wise one, [one perceives] the truth that is non-contradictory across all the scriptures.
O ocean of compassion, you must instruct us regarding the description of the creation wrought by Śiva, so that our minds may attain concentration here. (88)
Beholding him thus entreating the sages, the foremost of Śiva-yogis looked upon him with a gracious glance.
Revealing the secret essence of the meaning of all the scriptures, he says what was taught by the Guru: || 89 ||
Oh, leaders of sages, established in the supreme reality, listen with focused attention within yourselves!

You have taken up this question posed by you [and Bhavānī]... (* * * *). (Note: In the palm-leaf manuscript, these syllables were broken; as they could not be understood, they have been filled in with conjectures. ... [concluded]. 90.
For time is indeed beginningless; this entire collection of manifested phenomena was created by Śiva within his own heart.
By His command, those intermediate creations were performed in various places by Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and other principal deities;
likewise, they are found throughout the infinite Vedas, in various portions of the Purāṇas, and in the Āgamas.
Having examined the various distinctions of creation produced by each [of these], the Śāmbhava creation has been described as primary.
Relying upon the command of Maheśvara, let all [beings] beginning with Dhātṛ create; may the Lord [Iśvara] [govern] them.
Then Śiva bestows grace upon Maheśa, and they too take refuge in him, their own cause.
And the Śruti declares: "Rudra is superior to all," referring to the Lord who is to be served by the entire universe within his own self.
To him, the Śruti itself directly offers the merit arising from a thousand prostrations at all times. 94.
Therefore, unwavering devotion to Śiva alone is the cause of liberation for all the world.
Indeed, liberation is said to be freedom from illusion; who, then, could conquer it without the Lord? (95)
Having worshipped the Lord alone, all the gods attained the state of supreme identity with His form.
By the grace of this Śambhu, the gods headed by Viṣṇu have taken refuge in him;
indeed, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the others grant their own very positions to those who worship his feet.
Therein, in the pleasure of the union with the Liṅga, they do not [attain liberation]; therefore, these [beings] return once more to birth and death. || 97 ||
Those who, through the conviction that they are portions of the Lord, take refuge here upon Viṣṇu and the other principal deities by virtue of their own karmic power;
Having entered that abode by his command, they become devoted to the worship of Maheśvara.
They were brought together by that very Lord in the singular assembly for the experience of oneness with Sadāśiva.
Having entered into initiation when the dissolution has occurred, they attain lordship together with Him alone.
But those who, relying here upon independent causes of liberation, worship them—headed by Viṣṇu—[attain their respective goals].
Even after reaching that state, they quickly perish and return once more to the ocean of worldly existence;
yet, if those who have conquered their senses worship Viṣṇu and the other deities with a sattvic heart, perceiving them as the Supreme, they do not fall back.
Description of the Greatness of Śiva:
Even by means of various specific words, these [beings] perceive the Great Lord through the power of their latent impressions (saṃskāra). 101.
Then, in birth after birth, being steadfast in Śiva, they shall indeed gradually become Vīraśaivas.
In the end, they shall attain the state of oneness with Śiva; this is the secret hidden within all the Vedāntas.
Those who, out of a stubborn attachment to devotion to Śambhu and Śiva, revile Viṣṇu and the others.
And those who have been abandoned by them enter into blind darkness; of this there should be no doubt.
In the Purāṇic sections, however, Viṣṇu and others are revealed through devotion to the lotus feet of Śambhu.
Truly, those [devotees] are of great majesty and blessed; indeed, the Lord is pleased by the devotion of his devotees.
(104) When, in certain portions of the Bhāgavata and other texts, a deficiency was mentioned regarding Hari and the Lotus-born Brahmā—
That [state] of Rudra is to be known through the grace of some one among the innumerable Rudras. || 105 ||
Due to the predominance of the quality of tamas, even the gods such as Viṣṇu and Brahmā [worship] Śambhu, the Lord.
In some cases, they may appear contradictory; yet, when struck down by the Lord, this is not a fault for them, since they take refuge in virtue.
But for that Lord, the cause of all, [there is concern] for the multitudes of His own servants who are negligent in their respective duties.
Having distinguished and properly trained yourself, you must indeed bestow the gift of discernment upon those who alleviate suffering.
Therefore, the great ones are those who have attained superior fortune through the power of merit accumulated over many lifetimes.
They always take refuge in that Maheśvara, known as Sadāśiva, who is the cause of all causes.
Perceiving them as his devotees, they regard even Hari, Indra, Vidhātṛ, and the foremost of the gods with affection.
Those established in meditative absorption (samādhi) cause everything to dissolve into Maheśvara through the vision of non-duality;
such devotion to Śaṅkara belongs to the great-souled ones, while that of those of middling capacity on earth is due to their partial similarity with His portions.
Furthermore, O lords of sages, due to the power of their past actions, men may have devotion toward other [inferior] things. (110)
The castes and stages of life (varṇāśrama), proclaimed in the Śruti by the very command of Śiva, are well-known throughout the entire world;
yet all these are indeed attributes of the body, for they do not belong to the Self, which is omnipresent and non-dual. (111)
The command of that Maheśvara himself ordains the entire web of ritual actions for people possessed of ignorance and other defects;
it enjoins pure deeds and even prohibits dark deeds.
It ordains devotion, dispassion, and that action which is neither white nor black, as well as initiation, for the multitude of those seeking liberation.
When detachment becomes firm, having abandoned everything, one establishes oneself in the supreme state of identity with Śiva. || 113 ||

Having carefully considered his own qualification, the wise man, instructed by his guru, should take refuge in the meaning established by the scriptures through virtuous practice; once his mind is purified, he shall proceed upon the path of higher knowledge.
For even the command [of the scriptures] cannot be transgressed; thus it is established that one must abandon ritual action (karman).
Therefore, being detached and initiated into Śiva, he should cultivate devotion and then relinquish ritual action.

Just as Śiva is preeminently renowned as the Brāhmaṇa among all the social orders (varṇas), so too is this very Brāhmaṇa to be worshipped by Brāhmaṇas as the supreme among all, for he is indeed that Brāhmaṇa. 116.
He who is a Brāhmaṇa endowed with devotion to the Brāhmaṇa is to be known as such in two ways: by birth and by nature.
One devoid of devotion to him is not a Brāhmaṇa merely by birth; in this matter, the Brāhmaṇa himself is the authority.
O Brahmin, he who is pure by nature is alone a living embodiment of the scriptures here;
but a twice-born man who, despite his birth, is devoid of the reality of Śiva, is not considered a true Brāhmaṇa—this is our view.
A twice-born man attains the destination of his ancestors and others solely by performing the prescribed rites;
whereas one who is a Śaiva in name only, or one devoted to other deities, goes to their respective worlds and returns again to death.
The blessed Brāhmaṇa who knows Brahman and is established on the path of Śiva attains liberation;

even another, though by birth, if filled with devotion to Śiva, attains the state of a Brāhmaṇa and is liberated. (120) There can be no state of Śūdra for one devoted to the Lord, the Sovereign, who has taken recourse to the rite of initiation.
One who is uninitiated into the path of devotion to Śambhu becomes a dog-eater (outcaste) due to the offense against Śiva. || 121 ||
Śiva himself shall be the deity of the Brāhmaṇas; Janārdana is to be served by those born of the Kṣatriya lineage;
the Four-faced One (Brahmā) is to be worshipped by families of Vaiśyas; and indeed, the Śūdra is devoted to the worship of Gaṇeśvara.
Thus the Smṛti declares; this indeed is the intended meaning of that statement:
"Whichever overlord one worships, he shall surely possess the very nature of that [overlord]. (123)
Therefore, by virtue of merit, every person of all castes especially worships Śiva;
this is the description of the divisions of Kula, Akula, and Vīraśaiva.
By means of the special initiation (viśeṣadīkṣā), that practitioner is considered to be as rich in virtues as a Brāhmaṇa. 124.
Indeed, all these people, through the power of their commonality, become Śaivas who are solely intent upon Śiva.
By virtue of this special initiation, these castes on earth become Vīraśaivas. || 125 ||

Then, those foremost among the wandering ascetics—the Śiva-avadhūtas who have received the singular initiation into the state beyond all appearances, the self-restrained ones full of dispassion, and the lords among sages—truly purify the entire world. (126)

Indeed, Vīraśaivism is divided into two types—Kula and Akula—by those established in the Kula path. That which is resorted to by those for whom the Liṅga is the body (liṅgāṅgin), according to the method taught by Śiva, is Kula-Vīraśaivism.

Likewise, that which is called the "unfounded" (akula) lineage, having been divided from the [original] lineage, is to be worshipped by those who are devoted to the secrets of grace and signs, who have received initiation into that alone, who have taken wives, who worship Śiva, and who are endowed with virtuous conduct. || 128 ||

Indeed, this Vīraśaivism, established from time immemorial and taught by Śiva within this lineage of the Pramathas, attains renown in the world as being of two kinds; it is the cause of liberation according to the gradation of one’s qualities. (129)

The Śruti declares: "Even a dog-eater who clearly utters the name 'Śiva' is one who possesses true initiation; he is superior in merit. One should eat with him, speak with him, act with him, and likewise dwell with him. (130)
Therefore, for men who possess good character and whose nature is Śiva, there is no fault due to the abandonment of their family;
for the sake of protecting them, Śiva himself created this lineage of the mobile liṅga (jaṅgamaliṅga). 131.

This lineage of mobile [beings], established from time immemorial, was created by Śiva himself from his own head; therefore, the Lord, assuming the play of the mobile liṅga, protects his devotees by shielding them. 132.
Furthermore, in the Kali age, for the sake of rescuing the Śaiva tradition destroyed by base Buddhist communities, the Lord [appeared].
That very Lord shall descend, as well as these lords of bulls and others, just as before.
In that very way, that digit of consciousness (citkalikā), having descended, shall attain a state of aesthetic equilibrium (sāmarasya) with the Lord;
he shall become the six-faced one (Kārttikeya) with hidden clouds, and this hero shall be Maṇivālanātha.

Thus, this account of past events will likewise occur here during the Tiṣya age; O lords of sages, you should always contemplate this noble life-story of the Lord in your hearts. (135) [Conclusion of the Narrative]

Those established in the Vedic path are the most excellent; indeed, those established in Yoga are superior to them. Greater than they are the great ones devoted to Śiva, and the venerable Vīraśaivas are even superior to them.
(136) Those great ones of the Akula tradition, solely intent on initiation, are even superior to those [Vīraśaivas].
The illustrious ones, established in the state of non-appearance and dispassion, are renowned as having transcended the castes and stages of life through the sacred revelation.
Then those hosts [of Śiva], in order to establish the great Kula-vīra-śaivism upon the earth, descend into his lineages and, through their extraordinary intuition, reveal that reality. (138)
In the Kali age, there will arise those of great power within the lineage of Śiva and therein the Vīraśaiva tradition,
in order to protect the non-dual Śāmbhava doctrine from those born of the lineage cursed by Dadhīci.
Having heard the account of Mallamaguru as told by Sūta, those devotees of Śiva were filled with joy.
The supreme atoms,
with hundreds of heart-pleasing offerings such as rudrākṣa beads, ashes, fruits, bark garments, and betel rolls, performed prostrations before him.
Even those who have mastered the Vedas, by bearing the divine play of the Guru even once, have crossed the ocean of worldly existence and become fulfilled;
such were the disciples headed by the son of Bhṛgu, who attained Vīraśaivism.
They constantly offer praise, their state of being one with the desired life-force remaining unshakable.
[Thus, in the extensive narrative of the venerable Bhaviṣyat Purāṇa,
within the garland of twenty-five jewels of principles strung together by the aphorisms of the nectar-like teachings of Śrī Vīramāheśvara Amṛtānanda,
which conforms to the successive tradition of the words of the Pramatha hosts...]

The twenty-fifth chapter, titled "The Conclusion of the Narrative Concerning the Description of the Greatness of Vīraśaivism, Which Consists of the Concentration of the Mind of Maheśvarī Attained through the Grace of the Supreme Lord, Within the Divine Play of Prabhuliṅga, Whose Nature is to Lift Up People Submerged in the Impurities of the Kali Age."
May this be offered to the illustrious Supreme Lord.
Salutations to the illustrious Nandikeśvara.
Śrīḥ! Śrīḥ!
